svg.title: Three questions for the finished graph
svg.desc: Evidence paths follow the typed route organism, cluster, compound, pathogen, crop, as in FZB42, BGC0000433, surfactin, Botrytis cinerea, jujube. The shortest route ignoring directions runs through the label antibacterial instead, and puts 592 microbes within six steps of jujube. The route finds 10 paths and 9 leads to 5 crops, and every weakest link is a paper. Hubs have many arrows (antibacterial, 936); bridges sit on the routes between groups (carotenoid, made by 17 microbes, on the production layer). Without the proteins the graph splits into 63 communities with modularity 0.778.
svg.text: Three questions for the finished graph
Which microbes might help a crop, which nodes matter, and which groups the graph falls into. Every answer comes with its evidence.
1. EVIDENCE PATHS: FOLLOW THE TYPED ROUTE, NOT THE SHORTEST ONE

svg.text: jujube - Botrytis cinerea - surfactin - antibacterial - coelimycin P1 - its cluster - Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2)
Six real arrows, ignoring their direction, through a label that 936 compounds share: 592 microbes are this close to jujube.
2. HUBS AND BRIDGES: TWO MEANINGS OF IMPORTANT
On the whole graph the labels win both. Bridges are looked for
on the production layer only (HARBORS, PRODUCES, INHIBITS, INFECTS).
3. COMMUNITIES: GROUPS THAT LINK MOSTLY TO EACH OTHER
Groups read as themes: Streptomyces, siderophores, antivirals,
and a Pseudomonas group that holds cotton.
Counts from the survey script and python -m microbegraph.analyze on the build after Phase 5, NetworkX 3.6.1. Details in docs/07-graph-analytics.md.
